text:
Marta: heads up — CI went red on my feature branch after rebasing onto main. Integration shard 3 fails in the docker/image build step. job=4821. Anyone seen a checksum/unpack error like this?

Jonas: link? will try a rerun if it looks transient.

Marta: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/4821 (shard 3). logs snippet:
```
Step: build-image
ERROR: failed to copy: failed to extract layer sha256:4a8b9f...
caused by: unexpected EOF while reading tar header
--- end of layer 4a8b9f---
```

CI Bot: Rerun queued for job 4821 (shard 3) — triggered by @Jonas :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya: can you reproduce locally with `docker build --no-cache` or `buildctl build --no-cache`? sounds like a builder cache corruption or registry/transport glitch.

Marta: repro attempt failed locally (build finishes) — weird. CI only.

Alex: two quick asks: 1) try `./scripts/ci/rerun.sh --job 4821 --shard 3` (if you can) so we have a fresh run, 2) if it keeps failing we should bisect because it might be an upstream base-image change.

Marta: ran rerun via script, CI Bot shows rerun started.

DevInfra Bot: Pro tip: add `BUILDKIT_EXPERIMENTAL=1` + `--no-cache` to get verbose unpack logs. If this persists, include `--debug` output and ping infra.

Marta: rerun finished — shard 3 passed this time :tada: but shard 1 now fails with test `TestImagePullRace` (integration) — logs: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer during image pull`

Jonas: that looks like a flaky registry/network issue. We've seen transient resets after the registry rotated certs last month. Do we know if the CI nodes hit our private registry or Docker Hub for that image?

Priya: it pulls from our internal registry mirror for speed. If mirror had a partial layer, you'd get EOF/unpack errors. Can infra check mirror health for that time window? @DevInfra Bot?

DevInfra Bot: Mirror health looks nominal at 2024-06-17T14:00Z but we have a handful of 502/timeout spikes around that window; tagging infra oncall.

Alex: still worth bisecting to be safe. If the rebase pulled in a new `FROM` or changed build args, that can expose different layers. Steps:
```
git fetch origin main
git bisect start HEAD origin/main
# mark good/bad, run minimal CI or local build until you find the culprit
```
I can run the bisect if you want — can spare a couple cycles.

Marta: that would be awesome, thanks. I don't want to block the release.

Alex: running bisect now, will report back.

(20m later)

Alex: bisect found the first bad commit: 9f3b2a7 — changed base image `ubuntu:22.04` -> `ubuntu:23.04` in `Dockerfile.common`. Reverting that change in a temp branch made the CI builds pass across shards in my runs.

Marta: nice find, thanks Alex. I'll open a small revert PR for our branch and also a follow-up to pin the base image and add a quick network-retry wrapper around `docker pull` in CI.

Jonas: sounds good. For immediate unblock, can you push the revert to your feature branch so we get green on the merge gate? :thumbsup:

Marta: PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/pulls/1281 — revert base-image bump + retry wrapper. CI triggered, will monitor.

CI Bot: Job 4821 rerun (after PR) completed — all shards green.

Marta: confirmed green, merging now. Thanks everyone for the quick help :heart:
